clue.text: Drive off a green

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for the colour green

explanation.surface: Someone driving off a golf green, or chasing someone off the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like a golf term but gives VERT, green in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to ward it off or drive it away.

clue.text: Call in church to be excessively humble

indicators.note: in tells us the word for call sits inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to ring someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.surface: A churchgoer who answers the call to worship with too much grovelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RING inside CE, the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to cower or behave servilely, a show of exaggerated humility.

clue.text: Walked tiredly although Rita sped round

indicators.note: round suggests the letters of the two names and words are spun about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone trudged along wearily while Rita zipped around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges the letters of RITA and SPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge wearily from place to place.

clue.text: The name concocted for an inflammable gas

indicators.note: something concocted is cooked up or made up, so the letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist invents a name for a newly found flammable gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges the letters of THE and NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsh gas, the main part of natural gas, burns readily and is a classic example of a flammable gas.

clue.text: Type of train that needs a conductor to work?

definitions.text: Type of train that needs a conductor to work?

parts.words: Type of train that needs a conductor to work?
parts.note: the conductor seems to be the ticket inspector, but it is a wire carrying current that powers the train

explanation.surface: A train that cannot run without its guard on board.
explanation.walkthrough: A railway conductor checks tickets; an electrical conductor carries current, which this kind of train needs to move.
explanation.definitionFit: Such trains draw power through overhead wires or a live rail, both conductors of current.

clue.text: I had come up with an account of the detour

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, written ID
a version is one person's account of events

explanation.surface: Someone explains that they came up with their own story of the detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come up' turns ID round to DI, which comes before VERSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is a road detour set up when the usual route is closed.

clue.text: Never leaves off-always retaining its vigour

definitions.meaning: a plant that never drops its foliage, keeping green through winter
something that stays fresh and popular however long it lasts

explanation.surface: A tribute to someone who never stops and keeps all their energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly and pine keep their leaves all year, and a perennially popular song or star is called this too.

clue.text: Everybody at home is exhausted

parts.note: all means everybody
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: The whole family is at home, and worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all in is an informal idiom for being completely worn out.

clue.text: Was tense

definitions.meaning: the word was belongs to bygone time
a grammatical tense, the one for earlier events

explanation.surface: Someone recalls having felt nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervousness but is the grammar term; 'Was' is an example of that tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Was is the past tense of be, and the past is one of the grammatical tenses.

clue.text: Wave the cereal bowl

parts.note: bran is a cereal, the husk of grain eaten at breakfast
a dish is a bowl

explanation.surface: Someone waves at the breakfast bowl of cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' is a verb here, not a sea wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a weapon or object is to wave it about flourishingly.

clue.text: Tell her car crashed!

indicators.note: a crashed car is smashed up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An urgent message: tell her that her car has been in a crash!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' is William Tell, the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple off his son's head, not the verb. 'crashed' rearranges HER and CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the legendary Swiss bowman, the most famous example of a crack shot with a crossbow.

clue.text: Sort of pool tax

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Sort of pool tax' (4) for LESS: no parse gives LESS; the clue reads as a definition of CESS (a tax, perhaps 'poll' misread as 'pool'), so answer or clue is an OCR slip that cannot be confirmed without the grid

clue.text: One who is barely visible

parts.note: barely seems to mean hardly, but it means without clothes: someone seen in the bare

explanation.surface: A person who can only just be seen in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' means scarcely in the surface but 'in a bare state' in the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudist goes about unclothed, visible in a bare state.

clue.text: On being in control of a religious establishment

indicators.note: being in says the first word sits inside the word for control

parts.note: mastery is control or command over something
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of running a church institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' puts ON inside MASTERY; 'of' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A community of monks lives in this kind of religious house.

clue.text: Eat away at the metal bar in the centre

indicators.note: in places the word for bar inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: Rust eats away at a metal bar set in the middle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal bar' looks like one piece, but 'metal' belongs to the definition and 'bar' gives ROD, which goes inside CORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust and acid corrode metal, wearing it away by chemical action.

clue.text: Warmer in the house, cooler in the car

definitions.meaning: a domestic heater fixed to the wall
the engine part through which coolant is passed to lose heat

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that heats at home and chills on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the central-heating panel and the honeycombed engine part pass heat to the air.

clue.text: An infringement in rugby causing a series of effects

definitions.meaning: dropping the ball forward, an offence in rugby
a chain reaction, one consequence leading to the next

explanation.surface: A rugby foul that sets off a chain of consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' links the two definitions. In rugby union, a player who drops the ball forwards concedes a scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward fumble in rugby has this name, as does a domino-like chain of consequences, the 'knock-on effect'.

clue.text: Uniform colour?

parts.note: uniform seems to mean even or unvarying, but it means the dress of a service, here a sailor's

explanation.surface: A question about a paint that is the same shade all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' is an adjective in the surface but a noun in the reading: the dark shade worn by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval uniforms are a dark blue, which gave the shade its name.

clue.text: One in season showing mercy

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the season

parts.note: spring is a season
One gives A

explanation.surface: Someone who is lenient during a particular time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparing someone means letting them off, so sparing is merciful.

clue.text: Hindrance, of course

definitions.meaning: a race on a racecourse where weights are assigned to even out the runners

explanation.surface: A grumble that something is an obstacle, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but refers to a racecourse or golf course: a race with weights, or a golfer's stroke allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage is a burden, and on the racecourse it names a race where better horses carry extra weight.

clue.text: Censorious Roman turncoat

indicators.note: turn says the letters of the following word are turned about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stern Roman who switched sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turncoat' reads as one word for a traitor but splits into 'turn' (rearrange) and COAT. Cato the Elder, a Roman censor, was famous for strict morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Censor was renowned for severe moral criticism in republican Rome.

clue.text: Have a large portion of meat

indicators.note: portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to help yourself to a big serving of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'portion of' is the hidden-word signal, not a serving size.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf flesh is a meat served in dishes like schnitzel.

clue.text: Foreign girl almost in the saddle

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: astride means sitting with legs either side, as in the saddle

explanation.surface: A girl from abroad who has nearly mounted her horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E of ASTRIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a Scandinavian girl's name, so it suits a foreign girl.

clue.text: Baulk arrangement in Afghanistan

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A refusal to agree a deal somewhere in Afghanistan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges BAULK. The definition is loose: the capital city is a place in Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabul is the capital city of Afghanistan, so it is a place within that country.

clue.text: Finally Sal, upset, is taken in by a teetotaller

indicators.note: taken in by means the reversed name goes inside the letters for a teetotaller

parts.note: TT is short for teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sal, at the end, is upset and taken in by a non-drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses SAL to LAS; 'taken in by' puts it inside A + TT.
explanation.definitionFit: At last means after a long wait, in the end.

clue.text: True, short remnant is in the retort

indicators.note: is in places the word for a remnant inside the word for true

parts.note: real means true or genuine
a butt is a short leftover end, as of a cigarette

explanation.surface: A truthful aside that a scrap of something lies in the laboratory flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retort' suggests a lab vessel but is a sharp reply; 'is in' puts BUTT inside REAL, and 'the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a counter-argument, a reply that contradicts.

clue.text: Crime for which clergyman lost his head

indicators.note: lost his head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar who lost his head over a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost his head' drops the P of PARSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Without interest become liable to debts

parts.note: to incur a cost is to become liable to it
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A loan with no interest charged still makes you liable to debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' looks like a finance term but means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking curiosity shows no interest in things.
